new_symbol_range_suggestions.J2: 0 to 1e-1 for weak-to-moderate oblateness; J2=0 recovers the spherical parent limit
new_symbol_range_suggestions.R_eq: 1e3 to 1e9 depending on central body class; require r >= R_eq for exterior equatorial circular orbits

derivation_notes: For equatorial circular orbits around an oblate body, the leading external-field correction can be represented by the dimensionless loading J2*(R_eq/r)**2 acting inside the circular-frequency denominator. Using J2 as the only new independently varied input satisfies the one-new-degree-of-freedom limit, while R_eq remains a fixed dataset parameter that sets the distance scale where the correction becomes observable.
change_summary: Added a central-body oblateness quadrupole correction to the Kepler period using one new input, J2. This introduces a shape-dependent deviation from the pure r**(3/2) scaling at small orbital radius and recovers the parent law when oblateness vanishes or the orbit is far from the body.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: The central body's non-spherical mass distribution adds a quadrupole contribution to the exterior gravitational field, altering the circular-orbit period beyond a point-mass prediction.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: The added mechanism vanishes when J2=0 or becomes negligible when R_eq/r is small, reducing the period to the Kepler expression.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: At fixed M_c, two bodies with different J2 produce different orbital periods at the same r, with the difference largest for low-altitude equatorial orbits and fading for large r.

response_change.parent_relation: T depends only on r and M_c through T=2*pi*sqrt(r**3/(G*M_c)), so at fixed r and M_c the same period is predicted regardless of any environmental property of the central body.
response_change.child_relation: Include the central body's finite quadrupole-induced deviation from a point-mass potential for equatorial circular orbits, so T depends on both r and a new input describing central-body oblateness/size; the r-dependence is no longer a pure r^(3/2) law at fixed M_c.
response_change.observable_effect: For two central bodies with the same M_c but different oblateness or radius, the orbital period at the same r differs systematically, with the contrast strongest for low-altitude orbits and fading at large r.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the orbit is close enough to the central body that departures from a pure monopole field are not negligible, e.g. low-altitude orbits around an oblate rotating planet; the effect vanishes for nearly spherical bodies or for r much larger than the body's size.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, varying r can already reveal a departure from the exact Kepler slope at small r; in holdout, extending to more extreme close-in orbits or more oblate central bodies strengthens the same radius-dependent deviation rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of zero oblateness or when the orbital radius is large compared with the central-body size so only the monopole term remains important.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: The omitted effect depends on an independently variable property of the central body beyond total mass, such as its oblateness or equatorial radius; existing inputs r and M_c alone cannot distinguish two bodies with the same mass but different non-sphericity.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Quadrupole correction from central-body oblateness in the equatorial gravitational field
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Central-body oblateness produces a quadrupole correction to the gravitational field, modifying the inward acceleration required for a circular equatorial orbit and therefore the period-radius relation.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The new term combines multiple declared quantities into the dimensionless group J2*(R_eq/r)**2 and then applies a nonlinear map (1 - ...)**(-1/2), creating a radius-shape interaction rather than a simple global rescaling.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The central body is spherical and stationary.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The central body may be oblate, so its external field includes a leading quadrupole correction for equatorial circular orbits.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: J2 -> 0, or equivalently R_eq/r -> 0, recovers the parent expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compared at the same M_c, close-in equatorial orbits around more oblate bodies have systematically shifted periods relative to the pure Kepler prediction, while distant orbits collapse back onto the parent curve.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set predicts exactly the same T for bodies with equal M_c at the same r because it has no dependence on any shape variable. Retuning existing coefficients can only change the common Kepler scale, not produce one shared far-field relation together with body-specific close-in deviations across multiple oblateness conditions.

Changed target mapping: for equatorial circular orbits around bodies of equal M_c but different oblateness/size, the child predicts different T at the same r; equivalently, at fixed body shape the log-slope of T versus r bends away from the pure 3/2 Kepler value at small r and returns toward it far away. This is a true change in the scored T(r,...) mapping, not merely an auxiliary internal trajectory. Held fixed in the contrast: M_c and the orbital plane choice; varied: r and the newly introduced body-shape input. A single refit of the parent with only one shared G cannot reproduce both the far-field Kepler behavior and the close-in body-specific deviation across multiple shape conditions, because the parent lacks any handle for shape-dependent variation at fixed M_c. Admissible regime: near-circular low-altitude orbits around oblate planets or rapidly rotating stars; limitation: if all sampled bodies are nearly spherical or all orbits are very distant, the correction is too small to justify activation.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.c: 1e7 to 1e9 for synthetic benchmarks spanning finite propagation-speed scales; physical vacuum value is about 3e8

derivation_notes: The child model embeds a weak-field relativistic compactness factor into the coefficient of the existing oblateness process, so the J2-induced period correction now depends on G*M_c/(r*c**2) as well as on (R_eq/r)^2. In the weak-field limit G*M_c/(r*c**2) -> 0, the multiplicative relativistic factor tends to 1 and the parent expression is recovered exactly.
change_summary: Added a post-Newtonian compactness modulation to the existing oblateness correction by introducing the finite propagation-speed scale c as a new input. This creates a coupled r-M_c interaction in the scored period that the parent's fixed-environment mapping cannot match with one shared parameter set.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: Finite-speed general-relativistic monopole effects weakly modulate the existing oblateness contribution to the orbital period for exterior circular orbits around sufficiently compact bodies.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: The relativistic factor becomes unity in the weak-field limit G*M_c/(r*c**2) -> 0, equivalently c -> oo, recovering the parent expression exactly.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: For fixed shape parameters, residual period shifts become larger at smaller r and larger M_c through compactness, so bodies with different mass no longer follow one shared Newtonian-plus-J2 radius trend.

response_change.parent_relation: The period depends only on r and M_c through the Kepler factor multiplied by an oblateness correction set by fixed J2 and fixed R_eq; for any given central body shape, changing only r produces a single smooth radius-dependent scaling.
response_change.child_relation: Add the leading post-Newtonian relativistic correction from the central monopole, so the period depends on both the oblateness scale (R_eq/r)^2 and the compactness scale G*M_c/(r*c^2), creating a mixed response across r and M_c that is absent in the parent.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed r, increasing M_c shortens the Newtonian period but also strengthens a relativistic lengthening correction proportional to compactness; across bodies with different M_c, the T-versus-r curvature departs from the parent's purely Newtonian-plus-J2 form.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model includes oblateness but still assumes instantaneous Newtonian central attraction from the monopole, omitting the leading weak-field relativistic correction for circular orbits around compact massive bodies.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that the central attraction is purely Newtonian while keeping a circular, test-particle, exterior orbit around a stationary axisymmetric body.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: General-relativistic weak-field correction to circular orbital motion around the central mass, added on top of the existing quadrupole oblateness effect.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping is effectively a fixed-environment correction: once J2 and R_eq are fixed, T is just the Kepler period with one radius-only oblateness factor. A realistic next refinement is the leading relativistic monopole correction, which changes the scored mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. Vary r and M_c while holding the central body's shape parameters fixed. In the parent, all mass dependence enters through the single Kepler scaling M_c^(-1/2), with oblateness contributing only through J2(R_eq/r)^2. In the child, an additional compactness dependence G*M_c/(r*c^2) appears, so two systems with the same Newtonian timescale scaling but different compactness show different residual period shifts. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this across admissible conditions because J2 and R_eq control an r^-2-type shape correction, whereas the relativistic term follows a distinct mass-radius combination tied to compactness. The effect is scientifically admissible for exterior circular orbits around sufficiently compact bodies or at small enough radii; if all sampled systems are weak-field to extreme precision, the contrast may be too small to observe, which is a limitation of the regime rather than of the mechanism.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when compactness G*M_c/(r*c**2) is not asymptotically tiny but still below the circular-orbit existence limit, with weak-to-moderate oblateness correction so the orbit remains circular and the static approximation is meaningful; negligible in the far-field limit.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation over r and M_c already changes compactness; in holdout, smaller r or larger M_c extends the same compactness trend and exposes the stronger curvature of the exact relativistic mapping rather than a new force.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: As G*M_c/(r*c**2) -> 0, the refined relativistic factor expands back to the parent's weak-field form, recovering the parent law to leading order.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current equation includes relativity only through a low-order weak-field correction, which omits the known stronger nonlinear dependence of exact circular-orbit timing on compactness in a static spherically symmetric field.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The relativistic correction is adequately represented by the first-order weak-field factor (1 - 3*G*M_c/(r*c**2)) within the circular-orbit period formula.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Exact Schwarzschild circular-orbit kinematics make the period depend nonlinearly on compactness beyond first order, producing stronger bending of the period-radius relation near compact central masses.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent response maps T from r and M_c through a Newtonian r^(3/2)/sqrt(M_c) trend times a low-order multiplicative correction from oblateness and relativity. A realistic next refinement is to relax only the relativistic truncation already present, not to add a new force. Hold J2, R_eq, and c fixed and vary r and M_c: the parent predicts a single weak-field compactness dependence, whereas the child predicts a steeper increase in T as compactness grows. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the scored output T itself acquires different curvature versus the supplied inputs. The contrast is scientifically admissible for circular orbits outside the strong-field breakdown region; in the far field the effect becomes small and the parent is recovered. A single shared parent form cannot reproduce both the weak-field behavior and the stronger compactness-induced curvature across those conditions because its relativistic dependence is fixed to the first-order structure.

scenario_text: A small body follows a circular orbit around a much more massive spherical central body. Orbital radius and central mass are independently varied, and the target is the time required to complete one revolution. The orbital timescale is set solely by the balance between inward central attraction and the acceleration required for circular motion.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent treats the weak-field relativistic effect as a first-order factor in 3*G*M_c/(r*c**2), multiplied with the oblateness factor, so at fixed J2 it produces essentially one shared low-order curvature of T versus r and M_c.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the relativistic circular-orbit assumption from a truncated weak-field factor to the exact Schwarzschild circular-orbit dependence while keeping the same static circular-orbit setting; this changes how rapidly T bends as compactness G*M_c/(r*c**2) grows, especially at smaller r and larger M_c.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed J2 and R_eq, the period rises above the parent prediction more sharply as r decreases toward a few gravitational radii; the child shows stronger compactness-driven curvature in T(r,M_c) that a single parent parameterization cannot match simultaneously at weak and stronger compactness.

derivation_notes: The parent inserted oblateness as an external multiplicative correction to an otherwise Keplerian period. Here the equatorial J2 contribution is instead placed inside the circular-orbit force balance, where the equatorial radial acceleration from an axisymmetric quadrupole gives an effective factor 1 - 3*J2*(R_eq/r)**2 multiplying the monopole term, while the existing relativistic factor is retained.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption that oblateness only perturbs the period multiplicatively and to first order. The successor derives the orbital timescale from a J2-modified angular-frequency denominator, creating a non-separable interaction between radius, central mass, and oblateness strength.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The already-included oblateness effect is assumed to perturb the period multiplicatively and only to first order, instead of entering the force-balance denominator that sets orbital angular frequency.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Axisymmetric quadrupole gravity changes the radial derivative of the effective potential for circular equatorial motion, so the circular-orbit frequency is set by the monopole-plus-quadrupole force balance rather than by a separable period prefactor.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed J2 the correction is a separable multiplicative factor in compactness G*M_c/(r*c**2) and oblateness ratio (R_eq/r)**2, so varying M_c and r only changes T through those independent factors.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linearized oblateness factor with the exact circular-orbit balance in the J2-modified potential, making the period depend on M_c and r through a non-separable denominator containing both the monopole and quadrupole contributions.
response_change.observable_effect: For fixed J2 and R_eq, the slope of T versus r changes more strongly at smaller r than predicted by the parent because the J2 contribution enters inside the orbital-frequency balance rather than as an external linear prefactor; the discrepancy grows when both compactness and oblateness strength are simultaneously larger.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored mapping changes from a factorized prefactor correction to a denominator-level modulation of the orbital-frequency law, altering slopes and curvature across joint changes in r, M_c, and J2.

evolution_contract.assumption_after: The child computes the period from circular-orbit force balance with the J2 term inside the effective gravity.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: Hold J2 and R_eq fixed and vary r and M_c: the parent gives an approximately separable fractional J2 correction, while the child predicts that the J2-induced period increase steepens with decreasing r because the same denominator controlling orbital frequency now contains 1 - 3*J2*(R_eq/r)**2. The effect is most visible when both compactness G*M_c/(r*c**2) and oblateness_strength J2*(R_eq/r)**2 are appreciable, producing extra curvature in the scored T(r, M_c) mapping rather than only changing an auxiliary quantity.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce this across varied r and M_c because the parent keeps oblateness as a factorized prefactor multiplying the relativistic correction, whereas the child places oblateness inside the orbital-balance denominator. That changes the joint dependence of T on r and M_c, so one shared parent parameter set cannot match both weak-activation and strong joint-activation regimes without losing the radius-dependent curvature contrast.

change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that the J2 correction acts independently of compactness. The successor adds a mixed compactness-oblateness contribution inside the circular-balance factor, so the J2-induced change in period bends differently with radius for close-in orbits.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The quadrupole oblateness correction and relativistic compactness correction factorize independently in the circular-orbit period law.
assumption_audit.mechanism: In close orbits around an oblate body, the quadrupolar perturbation is sampled in a compact gravitational regime, so the effective circular-orbit frequency shift depends jointly on oblateness and compactness rather than through two fully separable factors.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces toward the parent when the mixed factor J2*(R_eq/r)**2*(G*M_c/(r*c**2)) is negligible, especially in the weak-field or nearly spherical limits.

response_change.parent_relation: The period depends only on radius and central mass through a single equatorial circular-orbit mapping, with oblateness represented by one fixed quadrupole factor and relativistic compactness depending only on r and M_c.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the equatorial-orbit assumption so the quadrupole contribution depends on the orbit's latitude relative to the symmetry axis; then the period keeps the same monotone base trend in r and M_c but acquires an r-dependent interaction with J2 through the geometric weighting of the quadrupole term.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed M_c and J2, two circular orbits at the same radius but different allowed orientation relative to the spin axis have different periods; the J2-induced deviation from the spherical law is stronger for equatorial than for non-equatorial circular orbits, and this contrast grows as (R_eq/r)^2 increases.

evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the equatorial-orbit limit, or when J2 -> 0 so orientation dependence disappears.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: For an axisymmetric oblate body, the quadrupole part of the gravitational potential depends on latitude; circular-orbit balance therefore changes with orbital orientation, not just with radius.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it makes the oblateness contribution depend jointly on the existing compactness and oblateness controls. A single global retuning of the parent J2 weighting cannot reproduce the resulting radius-dependent warping once close-in and farther-out conditions are fit simultaneously.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The orbit is exactly circular and effectively equatorial with respect to the oblate central body's symmetry axis.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The oblateness contribution is no longer treated as a fixed-environment equatorial factor and instead acquires joint dependence on the compactness sampled by the orbit.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when the mixed correction 3*J2*(R_eq/r)**2*(G*M_c/(r*c**2)) is negligible, especially for J2 -> 0 or G*M_c/(r*c**2) -> 0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response: one shared equatorial J2 weighting gives a unique period for each r and M_c once J2 is fixed. Child response: the J2-induced shift acquires extra radius-dependent curvature through its joint dependence on compactness and oblateness scale, serving as the retained signature of the omitted orientation sensitivity. Under the distinguishing condition of fixed M_c and J2 with decreasing r in the admissible regime where J2*(R_eq/r)^2 is appreciable, the child predicts a stronger close-in departure from the parent's single J2 radial weighting. This changes the scored T mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce the stated contrast because the parent contains only the fixed radial quadrupole factor 1 - 3*J2*(R_eq/r)**2 multiplied by an independent relativistic factor. Retuning existing parameters can only rescale the shared J2 effect globally; it cannot create the additional joint dependence on both J2*(R_eq/r)**2 and G*M_c/(r*c**2) needed to match the altered close-in versus farther-out response over the activation conditions.
